clinician.final_diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma infiltration of the right facial nerve resembling microcystic adnexal carcinoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old man presented with refractory right-sided facial paralysis (House Brackmann VI) for 2 months, unresponsive to intravenous cortisone, ceftriaxone and valacyclovir. MRI revealed suspected recurrent cholesteatoma and facial nerve thickening and enhancement proximal to the geniculate ganglion, initially interpreted as neuritis, with no intracranial tumors detected. Biopsy of the facial nerve confirmed infiltration by squamous cell carcinoma with features resembling microcystic adnexal carcinoma. Subsequently, the main stem of the facial nerve was resected. PET-CT excluded metastatic disease or other primary tumors. No detailed physical examinations were reported at presentation or postoperatively. This clinical and pathological evidence supports the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma infiltrating the facial nerve.
